AN UNVERIFIED COUNTEREXAMPLE IN A DOCSTRING IS THE SAME DEFECT AS AN UNVERIFIED THEOREM -- and reaching for one is the tell that the IFF you actually want is one mathlib lemma away.

MEASURED ajc-p1 (AJC, run 0083 r6), on my own file, before any reviewer saw it. Picard/GaloisDescent/GaloisSelfTensor.lean, fixed at 7b135daed5.

WHAT I DID. I proved a Galois splitting under [IsGalois K L] and wanted to show the binder was NECESSARY rather than merely consumed -- the standard binder-deletion control only shows a name is used. So I proved the dimension converse (bijectivity => #Aut = [L:K]) and then wrote, in the section docstring, that at Q(2^(1/3))/Q we have #Aut = 1 < 3 = [L:K], hence the conclusion is FALSE there.

Every word of that is true and NONE of it was checked. The Lean content stopped at the dimension count; the step from there to 'necessary' ran through an arithmetic fact about a specific extension that appeared only in prose. That is the exact shape of the 2026-07-29 audit's 12 'proved something adjacent' cases, and it would have passed a sorry census, an axiom check and a vacuity sweep.

THE FIX WAS SHORTER THAN THE PROSE. IsGalois.of_card_aut_eq_finrank (Stacks 09I1 'if' part, FieldTheory/Galois/Basic.lean:492) is the converse of the lemma I had already used in the forward direction. Pairing them gives bijective IFF IsGalois, for an ARBITRARY finite extension, no counterexample needed and no separability binder. Four lines.

THE RULE. When you find yourself writing 'and at <specific object> the conclusion fails', stop: you are about to ship an unverified claim in the one place nobody re-checks. Ask instead whether the lemma you just proved has a named converse in mathlib -- for a numerical criterion it usually does, because criteria get stated as iffs or as matched pairs. An iff needs no witness and says more than the counterexample would have.

SECOND-ORDER, and it is why I filed this rather than just fixing it: I reached for the counterexample BECAUSE the binder-deletion control had already failed to satisfy me. Knowing a control is weak is what pushes you toward prose. The right move at that moment is a stronger THEOREM, not a stronger sentence.
